one_line: Anonymous early Magadhan stone-masons and laborers who raised the great dry-stone fortifications around ancient Rajagriha in the 6th century BCE.

appearance.age_look: Early 30s, lean but strong build with visibly worked muscles from heavy manual labour.
appearance.face: Oval face, medium-brown Gangetic plains complexion, sun-worn with light freckles and a few old scars; straight nose, strong jaw, and calloused hands often touching his belt; default expression calm, focused, with determined eyes that suggest quiet pride in his craft.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair gathered into a short topknot at the crown, sides and back trimmed to mid-neck; a narrow off-white cloth headband wrapped around the forehead to catch sweat, knotted at the back with small tails hanging down.
appearance.costume: He wears a knee-length unstitched lower garment (dhoti-style wrap) of coarse undyed off-white cotton, pleated and tied firmly at the waist, with a simple narrow brown woven belt; his upper body is covered by a light, short-sleeved, plain brown cotton tunic (early stitched garment, loose and practical) reaching mid-thigh with a round slit neck; over one shoulder he drapes a dusty grey-beige cotton angavastra-style cloth he can use as a shawl or to pad his shoulder when carrying stones; his feet are in simple dark brown leather sandals with thong straps; accessories are minimal—small plain copper ear-studs and a single thin copper bangle on his right wrist; the textiles are plain-weave, slightly rough, with faint vertical striping in the tunic from the loom, no later-period ornamentation or embroidery.
appearance.signature: A long wooden lever-pole about his own height, slightly darker at the ends from use, lashed with simple fiber rope at one end and paired with a flat rectangular stone chisel tucked into his belt, representing his work lifting and fitting the massive undressed stones of the Cyclopean Wall.

ref_desc: A lean early-30s Magadhan stone-mason with medium-brown skin, black hair in a short topknot with an off-white headband, wearing an off-white dhoti, brown short-sleeved tunic, grey-beige shoulder cloth, dark brown sandals, and carrying a wooden lever-pole and stone chisel in earthy browns and off-whites.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of a 6th-century BCE early Magadhan stone-mason from Rajgir: a lean, strong man in his early 30s with medium-brown Gangetic plains complexion, sun-worn oval face, straight nose, strong jaw, and calm, determined eyes; his black hair is gathered into a short topknot at the crown, with the sides and back to mid-neck, and a narrow off-white cloth headband wrapped around his forehead and knotted at the back. Dress him in an off-white knee-length dhoti-style wrap of coarse cotton, pleated and tied at the waist, and a plain brown short-sleeved cotton tunic reaching mid-thigh with a simple round slit neck, the fabric slightly rough with faint vertical loom stripes, plus a dusty grey-beige cotton cloth draped over one shoulder like an angavastra that can pad his shoulder when carrying stones. Give him simple dark brown leather sandals, a thin copper bangle on his right wrist, and small plain copper ear-studs, with visible calloused hands and forearms. His signature tools are a long wooden lever-pole about his height, darker at the ends from use, held in one hand, and a flat rectangular stone chisel tucked into his woven brown belt; keep colours in earthy off-whites, browns, grey-beige and dark wood tones. Show front, side, and back views consistent with this description so the same historically grounded, modestly dressed builder can be redrawn in many panels, emphasizing his practical worker’s outfit and the lever-pole and chisel as his defining props.
